reason: 'Sub' says the value holds only roughly. Squarrose (spreading sharply from the axis) has no term of its own, so the nearest existing value is PATO spreading, as was done for 'divergent'.
This is the absence of 'appendage', which was rejected as a generic part (it needs the organ it belongs to), and 'appendaged' was rejected too. An absence of an undefined part cannot be annotated.
Geniculate is mapped to PATO bent (rule C191), and bigeniculate is bent like a knee twice. The two bends can only be kept as a count modifier, because a bend is not a PO part.
Non-articulate = without a joint at which the pedicel, fruit or stem separates. This negates FLOPO jointed, in the same form as unlobed and indehiscent.
Same as the rule for 'crateriform' (C310). Crater-like glands and apices are bowl-shaped.
Bulbiferous = bearing bulbils, in the axils or in place of flowers. The bearer class bulbil FLOPO_0986055 already exists; the form follows stoloniferous.
Half-moon-shaped fruits, sori and appendages are crescentic, as in the rule for 'lunate' (C314). PATO semicircular (PATO_0002232) would be the reading only where a flora clearly means a half-disc.
Leaves and hairs that are 'harsh to the touch' are rough with short stiff points, i.e. scabrous. 'Flower harsh to honeylike' is a smell and is left out of the rule.
Aristate = with an awn (rule C207). 'Long' is increased length (PATO_0000573) of the awn, which goes to the awn as the substituted bearer, not into a new term.

label: amphibious
definition: A positional quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its growing both in water and on wet ground, often in a different form in each. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991112 aquatic and FLOPO:0991111 terrestrial; probably outside PATO's scope (where an organism lives).
reason: A common habit in floras that neither aquatic nor terrestrial covers alone. Using both would read as two contradictory states.

label: trimorphic
definition: A morphological quality inhering in a set of homologous plant structures by virtue of its members occurring in three distinguishable forms. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991092 dimorphic; trimorphic flowers or styles are tristylous, a kind of FLOPO:0991137 heterostylous.
reason: Floras use it of fern leaves (sterile, fertile, intermediate) and of tristylous flowers. It parallels the existing dimorphic class and has no PATO term.

label: dextrorse
definition: A torsioned quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's twisting, twining or overlapping in a right-handed helix. NOTE: Authors disagree on which direction 'dextrorse' names; PATO:0002203 right handedness is a behaviour. Needs a sinistrorse sibling.
reason: A real quality of twining stems, twisted setae and peristome teeth, and contorted corolla lobes, with no PATO term. Confidence is low because the direction convention differs between floras.

label: prehensile
definition: A climbing quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's coiling round a support and gripping it, as a tendril or twining petiole does.
reason: Said of petioles, rachises, branches and tendrils that act as climbing organs. FLOPO climbing is about the whole plant's habit; this is the grasping organ.
This describes the effect on whoever touches the hairs or fruit, not a feature of the plant part. Earlier, 'stinging' was also left without a term.

label: irregularly dehiscent
definition: A structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's opening at maturity by irregular breaks in its wall, not along a definite line or pore. NOTE: Not a child of FLOPO:0991149 dehiscent, whose definition requires a definite line or pore; PATO:0040044 ruptured is damage.
reason: FLOPO dehiscent requires a definite line, so dehiscent plus an 'irregular' modifier would contradict its definition. This is a distinct, common fruit character.
A plain negation of PATO recurved. Where stated ('at tip', 'apex'), the region goes in the part-of-bearer slot.

A weak or partial red colour. The colour backbone maps 'flushed with pink' to its level-1 hue in the same way. 'Tinged' is a degree modifier, and the region ('abaxially', 'distally') goes in the part-of-bearer slot.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: cuneate PATO_0001955 to attenuate PATO_0001982)
reason: A hyphenated compound of two base shapes, between wedge-shaped and gradually tapering. It is handled as a continuum, like ovate-lanceolate.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: obovoid FLOPO:0991025 to elliptic PATO_0000947)
reason: A compound of two solid shapes, both with terms ('ellipsoid' is a synonym of PATO elliptic). It is handled as a continuum, like ovate-lanceolate.
Scandent = climbing. 'Semi' marks a partly climbing, scrambling habit, which is an approximate value in the same way as 'sub'.

target: new: two values of one bearer (ovate FLOPO:0991024 and obtuse PATO_0001935 at the apex)
reason: Not a continuum: the outline is ovate and the apex is obtuse, and both hold. This is the same form as 'obliquely ovate'.
Palmately veined = three or more primary veins radiating from one point at the base, which is PATO actinodromous. '3–5-palmatinervé' also gives a vein count via docs/odp/03-count-of-parts.md.
A well-marked midrib, vein network or crest is clearly visible, as in the rules for distinct, evident and obvious (C176, C323, C324).
What 'ray' means changes with the bearer: the arms of a stellate hair, the rays of an umbel or a valve, or ray florets (already FLOPO:0991194 radiate). 'n-rayed' counts a part that has no class.
A colour comparison without the part it is compared with, as for 'paler' and 'lighter' (C241, C248). Where the other part is named ('than body'), docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md applies.
Not apparent = not clearly visible, the opposite of the rule for 'evident'. This matches the rules for obscure and indistinct (C174, C175).

target: new: two values of one bearer (rhomboid PATO_0001938 and asymmetrical PATO_0000616)
reason: The outline is rhombic and the sides are unequal (oblique = inequilateral), so both values hold, the same form as 'obliquely ovate'.
A tussock is a dense tuft of shoots growing from the base, which is FLOPO caespitose (synonyms tufted, clump-forming). 'Mats' is FLOPO:0991010 mat-forming.
Nearly opposite: inserted at slightly different levels on the axis. This is an approximate value of opposite, in the same way as suborbicular.

reason: 'Arranged in 1 or 2 rows' is a count of rows, which the -seriate value terms note should be a shared counted-arrangement expression. A bare 'in rows' gives no number and stays unresolved.
